historical_reviews.deepseek: Changes one-GPU source scope into an eight-process command and omits package pinning/rollback.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Restores exact NCCL package versions, -g1/8..128M sweep and controlled build/run.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row278 owns the eight-GPU all-reduce/all-to-all fabric benchmark; this row is a package installation plus single-GPU NCCL smoke.

original_test_intent: Install the exact NCCL 2.19.3 CUDA 12.2 runtime/development packages, build approved nccl-tests, and verify a selected GPU can complete the source-defined 8-byte to 128-MiB all-reduce smoke without errors.
original_method: Verify OS/arch, driver/CUDA ABI and authenticated package repository; inventory package/library state and rollback; pin nccl-tests commit/build flags; map intended GPU UUID/BDF to -g1 environment; preserve baseline/drain jobs; install approved packages and build in isolated path; run tracked exact sweep; capture per-size alg/bus bandwidth, errors/exit and telemetry; verify packages/GPU/app health and rollback readiness.
manual_activity: Software owner approves repository/ABI/source/GPU/oracle and rollback; operator approves package change and load; agent may install/build/run the exact smoke after gates pass.
required_inputs: Authenticated NCCL package repository and exact package hashes
Compatible OS/arch, driver and CUDA 12.2 ABI
PASS/error and optional performance threshold for the sweep
safety_requirements: Do not change shared NCCL/CUDA packages without rollback
Never substitute mpirun -np8 or multi-GPU scope
Do not clone moving HEAD or embed credentials
Track build/benchmark and abort on NCCL/XID/thermal/power anomaly
No automatic retry, GPU reset or improvised library changes
agent_execution_scope: Capture package baseline, install/build approved artifacts
Run exact single-GPU sweep and collect metrics/errors/health

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek's `mpirun -np 8` changes the source's explicit `-g 1` single-GPU test and is rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After pinned package/source installation, run exact `./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 128M -f 2 -g 1` on the mapped GPU and record every size row, errors and benchmark exit.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NCCL 2.19.3 CUDA 12.2, -b8/-e128M/-f2/-g1 and 60-minute estimates are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an apt/build transaction manifest and bind one mapped GPU to complete per-size nccl-tests output, package/library state and health evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes package ABI and GPU identity reproducible while preserving the intentionally single-GPU scope.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: This is not proof of multi-GPU NCCL transport; that remains row278.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Package changes can alter applications system-wide even though benchmark scope is one GPU.

project_override_considerations: Software owner defines repository trust, exact nccl-tests revision and whether PASS is zero errors/exit or also a minimum bandwidth curve.
expected_evidence: Pre/post driver/CUDA/NCCL/library inventory and rollback artifact
GPU UUID/BDF/-g1 mapping and exact argv
Complete per-size algBW/busBW/error output and exit
Telemetry plus dmesg/XID/PCIe/BMC/SEL deltas, cleanup/package health and verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master consistently defines pinned NCCL packages, a build and a one-GPU all-reduce smoke; DeepSeek's NP8 command is non-authoritative scope expansion.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Packages, source and acceptance inputs are provisionable; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Preserves exact single-GPU smoke and package installation coverage while preventing an invented multi-GPU substitution.
independent_technical_reasoning: NCCL can execute a one-rank collective for software/API smoke even though it does not exercise inter-GPU transport. Package ABI compatibility and library path state therefore matter as much as benchmark output. Changing to eight MPI ranks would test different topology and resources and could conceal whether the source installation itself was validated.
